summary: The People pillar of the World Economic Forum's Stakeholder Capitalism Metrics: dignity and equality, health and well-being, and skills for the future. It has 6 core and 9 expanded metrics.

disclosures.title: Dignity and equality: Diversity and inclusion (%)

questions.text: Does your company track the composition of its employees by employee category (e.g. senior management, professionals, operations)?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 405-1(b). Report yes if you break down headcount by employee category.

questions.text: How many employees did your company have at the end of the reporting period?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 405-1(b). Total headcount. Use the same count as the base for the percentages in the next questions.

questions.text: What percentage of employees in each employee category is under 30 years old?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 405-1(b). Give the percentage per employee category (share of that category, 0-100). Under-30 age group.

questions.text: What percentage of employees in each employee category is aged 30 to 50?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 405-1(b). Percentage per employee category aged 30-50.

questions.text: What percentage of employees in each employee category is over 50 years old?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 405-1(b). Percentage per employee category over 50.

questions.text: What percentage of employees in each employee category is women?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 405-1(b). Percentage of women per employee category (share of that category).

questions.text: What percentage of employees in each employee category is men?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 405-1(b). Percentage of men per employee category (share of that category).

questions.text: What percentage of employees in each employee category belongs to an ethnic minority or other under-represented group?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 405-1(b). Other indicators of diversity, e.g. ethnicity. State the group definition used in notes.

questions.text: Which other indicators of diversity does your company track among employees?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 405-1(b). Select all that you track and can report.

questions.text: Which employee categories does your company use when comparing pay?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: Adapted from GRI 405-2. List the categories (e.g. management, professional, operations) used to compare basic salary and remuneration.

questions.text: Which significant locations of operation does your company include when comparing pay?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: Adapted from GRI 405-2. List the locations (country/site) that are significant. Used as the reporting boundary.

questions.text: What is the ratio of the basic salary of women to men for each employee category and significant location?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: Adapted from GRI 405-2. Ratio = women's basic salary / men's basic salary (1.0 = equal). Report per category and location.

questions.text: What is the ratio of the total remuneration of women to men for each employee category and significant location?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: Adapted from GRI 405-2. Remuneration = basic salary plus bonuses, allowances, overtime and other cash/benefits. Ratio of women to men.

questions.text: What is the ratio of the basic salary of minor ethnic groups to major ethnic groups for each employee category and significant location?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: Adapted from GRI 405-2. Ratio of minor to major ethnic group basic salary (1.0 = equal), if you collect ethnicity data.

questions.text: What is the ratio of the total remuneration of minor ethnic groups to major ethnic groups for each employee category and significant location?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: Adapted from GRI 405-2. Ratio of total remuneration, minor to major ethnic groups.

questions.text: Which other equality areas does your company consider relevant for pay comparison?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: Adapted from GRI 405-2. E.g. disability, age, nationality. Describe the group compared and the ratio found.

questions.text: What is the standard entry-level wage for women at your company?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 202-1, UK Companies (Miscellaneous Reporting) Regulations 2018, Dodd-Frank Act. Local currency per hour/month; state the period used. Use the standard entry-level wage, not trainee or intern rates.

questions.text: What is the standard entry-level wage for men at your company?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 202-1, UK Companies (Miscellaneous Reporting) Regulations 2018, Dodd-Frank Act. Same currency and period as for women.

questions.text: What is the local minimum wage in your main locations of operation?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 202-1, UK Companies (Miscellaneous Reporting) Regulations 2018, Dodd-Frank Act. Same currency and period. If several locations, give the main one and list others in notes.

questions.text: What is the ratio of the entry-level wage for women to the local minimum wage?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 202-1, UK Companies (Miscellaneous Reporting) Regulations 2018, Dodd-Frank Act. Ratio = entry-level wage for women / local minimum wage.

questions.text: What is the ratio of the entry-level wage for men to the local minimum wage?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 202-1, UK Companies (Miscellaneous Reporting) Regulations 2018, Dodd-Frank Act. Ratio = entry-level wage for men / local minimum wage.

questions.text: What was the CEO's total annual compensation?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 202-1, UK Companies (Miscellaneous Reporting) Regulations 2018, Dodd-Frank Act. Include salary, bonus, stock, options and other pay for the reporting period.

questions.text: What was the median total annual compensation of all employees, excluding the CEO?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 202-1, UK Companies (Miscellaneous Reporting) Regulations 2018, Dodd-Frank Act. Median (middle value), not average. Use the same period and currency as for the CEO.

questions.text: What is the ratio of the CEO's total annual compensation to the median employee's total annual compensation?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 202-1, UK Companies (Miscellaneous Reporting) Regulations 2018, Dodd-Frank Act. Ratio = CEO total annual compensation / median total annual compensation of all other employees.

disclosures.title: Dignity and equality: Risk for incidents of child, forced or compulsory labour

questions.text: Does your company have any operations considered to be at significant risk for child labour?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 408-1(b), GRI 409. Consider type of operation (e.g. manufacturing plant) and country or area of operation.

questions.text: Does your company have any operations considered to be at significant risk for forced or compulsory labour?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 408-1(b), GRI 409. Same considerations as child labour risk.

questions.text: Does your company have any suppliers considered to be at significant risk for child labour?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 408-1(b), GRI 409. Consider type of supplier and country or area where they operate.

questions.text: Does your company have any suppliers considered to be at significant risk for forced or compulsory labour?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 408-1(b), GRI 409. Same considerations as child labour risk.

questions.text: Which types of operation or supplier are considered at risk?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 408-1(b), GRI 409. E.g. manufacturing plant, agriculture, mining, contract labour. Explain why they are considered at risk.

questions.text: Which countries or geographic areas with operations or suppliers are considered at risk?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 408-1(b), GRI 409. List the countries or areas and say whether they relate to operations, suppliers or both.

disclosures.title: Health and well-being: Health and safety (%)

questions.text: How many work-related fatalities occurred among employees and workers in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-9(a & b), GRI 403-6(a). Deaths resulting from work-related injury.

questions.text: What was the rate of work-related fatalities?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-9(a & b), GRI 403-6(a). Rate = fatalities / hours worked x 200,000 (or x 1,000,000; state which).

questions.text: How many high-consequence work-related injuries (excluding fatalities) occurred?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-9(a & b), GRI 403-6(a). Injuries from which the worker cannot, or is not expected to, recover fully within 6 months.

questions.text: What was the rate of high-consequence work-related injuries?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-9(a & b), GRI 403-6(a). Rate = number / hours worked x 200,000 (or x 1,000,000; state which).

questions.text: How many recordable work-related injuries occurred?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-9(a & b), GRI 403-6(a). All work-related injuries that must be recorded under local law or your system.

questions.text: What was the rate of recordable work-related injuries?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-9(a & b), GRI 403-6(a). Rate = number / hours worked x 200,000 (or x 1,000,000; state which).

questions.text: What were the main types of work-related injury?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-9(a & b), GRI 403-6(a). E.g. cuts, falls, burns, strains, crush injuries.

questions.text: How many hours were worked in total by employees and workers in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-9(a & b), GRI 403-6(a). Total hours worked; the base for all injury rates above.

questions.text: Does your company help employees and workers access non-occupational medical and healthcare services?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-9(a & b), GRI 403-6(a). E.g. health insurance, on-site clinic, referral programs.

questions.text: Which non-occupational medical and healthcare services does your company help workers access?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-9(a & b), GRI 403-6(a). Describe how access is facilitated and the scope (services covered).

questions.text: Which groups of employees and workers have access to these healthcare services?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-9(a & b), GRI 403-6(a). Say who is covered: full-time, part-time, contractors, family members, etc.

disclosures.title: Skills for the future: Training provided (#)

questions.text: What was the total number of training hours provided to employees in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: GRI 404-1, SASB HC0101-15. Sum of training hours for all employees.

questions.text: What was the average hours of training per employee in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: GRI 404-1, SASB HC0101-15. Total training hours / total number of employees.

questions.text: What was the average hours of training per female employee?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: GRI 404-1, SASB HC0101-15. Training hours of female employees / number of female employees.

questions.text: What was the average hours of training per male employee?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: GRI 404-1, SASB HC0101-15. Training hours of male employees / number of male employees.

questions.text: What was the average hours of training per employee in each employee category?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: GRI 404-1, SASB HC0101-15. Report per category (e.g. senior management, professionals, operations).

questions.text: What was the total training and development expenditure in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: GRI 404-1, SASB HC0101-15. Include course fees, trainer costs, materials and training-related travel; state currency.

questions.text: What was the average training and development expenditure per full-time employee?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: GRI 404-1, SASB HC0101-15. Total training and development expenditure / number of full-time employees; state currency.

questions.text: What is the mean pay gap in basic salary between women and men among full-time relevant employees?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: Adapted from UK Government guidance on gender and ethnicity pay gap reporting, GRI 102-38. Percentage gap = (men's mean - women's mean) / men's mean x 100. Company level or by significant location.

questions.text: What is the mean pay gap in total remuneration between women and men among full-time relevant employees?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: Adapted from UK Government guidance on gender and ethnicity pay gap reporting, GRI 102-38. Remuneration includes bonuses and allowances. Same formula as basic salary.

questions.text: What is the mean pay gap in basic salary between minority ethnic and other employees (e.g. BAME to non-BAME)?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: Adapted from UK Government guidance on gender and ethnicity pay gap reporting, GRI 102-38. Percentage gap for another indicator of diversity; state the groups compared.

questions.text: Is the pay gap reported at company level or by significant location of operation?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: Adapted from UK Government guidance on gender and ethnicity pay gap reporting, GRI 102-38. Pick the level used for the figures above.

questions.text: What is the ratio of total annual compensation of the highest-paid individual to the median employee in each country of significant operations?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: Adapted from UK Government guidance on gender and ethnicity pay gap reporting, GRI 102-38. Ratio = highest-paid individual / median of all other employees in the same country. Give one ratio per country.

disclosures.title: Dignity and equality: Discrimination and harassment incidents (#) and the total amount of monetary losses ($)

questions.text: How many incidents of discrimination occurred in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 406-1, SASB FB-FR-310a.4. Total confirmed or reported incidents of discrimination.

questions.text: How many incidents of harassment occurred in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 406-1, SASB FB-FR-310a.4. Total confirmed or reported incidents of harassment.

questions.text: What is the status of these incidents?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 406-1, SASB FB-FR-310a.4. E.g. under review, remediation underway, resolved, no longer subject to action.

questions.text: What actions has your company taken in response to these incidents?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 406-1, SASB FB-FR-310a.4. E.g. disciplinary action, training, policy changes, remediation.

questions.text: What were the total monetary losses from legal proceedings associated with law violations?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 406-1, SASB FB-FR-310a.4. Fines, settlements and legal costs for law violations; state currency.

questions.text: What were the total monetary losses from legal proceedings associated with employment discrimination?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 406-1, SASB FB-FR-310a.4. Settlements, fines and legal costs; state currency.

disclosures.title: Dignity and equality: Human rights review, grievance impact and modern slavery (#, %)

questions.text: How many operations were subject to human rights reviews or human rights impact assessments?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 412-1, UN Guiding Principles, GRI 408-1(a), GRI 409-1, WDI 7.5. Count in the reporting period.

questions.text: What percentage of operations were subject to human rights reviews or impact assessments?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 412-1, UN Guiding Principles, GRI 408-1(a), GRI 409-1, WDI 7.5. Operations reviewed / total operations x 100.

questions.text: In which countries were human rights reviews or impact assessments carried out?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 412-1, UN Guiding Principles, GRI 408-1(a), GRI 409-1, WDI 7.5. List the countries (report by country).

questions.text: How many grievances related to salient human rights issues were reported?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 412-1, UN Guiding Principles, GRI 408-1(a), GRI 409-1, WDI 7.5. Count in the reporting period.

questions.text: What types of human rights grievances were reported?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 412-1, UN Guiding Principles, GRI 408-1(a), GRI 409-1, WDI 7.5. E.g. discrimination, working hours, freedom of association, child labour.

questions.text: What impacts resulted from these grievances?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 412-1, UN Guiding Principles, GRI 408-1(a), GRI 409-1, WDI 7.5. Explain the impacts on people and on the company.

questions.text: How many operations are considered at significant risk for child labour, forced or compulsory labour?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 412-1, UN Guiding Principles, GRI 408-1(a), GRI 409-1, WDI 7.5. Count of operations at risk.

questions.text: What percentage of operations are considered at significant risk for child labour, forced or compulsory labour?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 412-1, UN Guiding Principles, GRI 408-1(a), GRI 409-1, WDI 7.5. At-risk operations / total operations x 100.

questions.text: How many suppliers are considered at significant risk for child labour, forced or compulsory labour?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 412-1, UN Guiding Principles, GRI 408-1(a), GRI 409-1, WDI 7.5. Count of suppliers at risk.

questions.text: What percentage of suppliers are considered at significant risk for child labour, forced or compulsory labour?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 412-1, UN Guiding Principles, GRI 408-1(a), GRI 409-1, WDI 7.5. At-risk suppliers / total suppliers x 100.

questions.text: Which types of operation or supplier, and which countries or areas, are considered at risk?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 412-1, UN Guiding Principles, GRI 408-1(a), GRI 409-1, WDI 7.5. Type of operation (e.g. manufacturing plant) or supplier, and countries or areas considered at risk.

questions.text: Does your company compare its wages with the living wage in the places where it operates?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: MIT Living Wage Tool, EPIC Report, IMP. Living wage = pay needed to meet basic needs locally (e.g. MIT Living Wage Tool).

questions.text: In which states or localities does your company operate?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: MIT Living Wage Tool, EPIC Report, IMP. List the places used for the living wage comparison.

questions.text: What percentage of employees are paid at or above the living wage?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: MIT Living Wage Tool, EPIC Report, IMP. Employees paid at or above local living wage / total employees x 100.

questions.text: What percentage of contractors are paid at or above the living wage?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: MIT Living Wage Tool, EPIC Report, IMP. Contractors paid at or above local living wage / total contractors x 100.

questions.text: What is the lowest wage paid to employees compared with the living wage in each location?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: MIT Living Wage Tool, EPIC Report, IMP. Give lowest current wage as a percentage of the living wage (100 = equal).

questions.text: Which living wage source or tool does your company use?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: MIT Living Wage Tool, EPIC Report, IMP. E.g. MIT Living Wage Tool, local benchmark.

disclosures.title: Dignity and equality: Annual total compensation ratio

questions.text: Which countries are your significant operations?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 102-38. The countries for which you report the ratio.

questions.text: What is the annual total compensation of the highest-paid individual in each country of significant operations?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 102-38. Salary, bonus, stock, benefits; state currency per country.

questions.text: What is the median annual total compensation of all other employees in each country of significant operations?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 102-38. Median excluding the highest-paid individual, in the same country and currency.

questions.text: What is the ratio of the highest-paid individual's compensation to the median employee in each country?
questions.hint: Dignity and equality · Source: GRI 102-38. Ratio = highest-paid / median of all other employees in that country.

disclosures.title: Health and well-being: Monetized impacts of work-related incidents on organization (#, $)

questions.text: How many occupational incidents occurred, by type of incident?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: Adapted indicator based on European Commission, Safe Work Australia. Number of incidents per type (e.g. injury, illness, fatality).

questions.text: What was the direct cost per incident for healthcare?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: Adapted indicator based on European Commission, Safe Work Australia. Average healthcare cost per incident; state currency.

questions.text: What was the direct cost per incident for compensation paid to employees?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: Adapted indicator based on European Commission, Safe Work Australia. Average compensation cost per incident.

questions.text: What was the direct cost per incident for property damage?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: Adapted indicator based on European Commission, Safe Work Australia. Average property damage cost per incident.

questions.text: What were the total actions and fines from regulators for work-related incidents?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: Adapted indicator based on European Commission, Safe Work Australia. Total fines and regulator-driven action costs.

questions.text: What was the total monetized cost of work-related incidents to your company?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: Adapted indicator based on European Commission, Safe Work Australia. Number of incidents of each type x direct cost per incident, summed across types.

questions.text: How many fatalities resulted from work-related ill-health?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-10(a & b), GRI 403-2(a), Embankment Project. Employees and workers, reporting period.

questions.text: What was the rate of fatalities from work-related ill-health?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-10(a & b), GRI 403-2(a), Embankment Project. Rate = fatalities / hours worked x 200,000 (or x 1,000,000; state which).

questions.text: How many cases of recordable work-related ill-health were there?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-10(a & b), GRI 403-2(a), Embankment Project. Cases recorded under local law or your system.

questions.text: What were the main types of work-related ill-health?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-10(a & b), GRI 403-2(a), Embankment Project. E.g. musculoskeletal disorders, stress, hearing loss, respiratory disease.

questions.text: Does your company run best-practice health and well-being programs?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-10(a & b), GRI 403-2(a), Embankment Project. Programs that reduce absenteeism and improve productivity.

questions.text: What percentage of employees participate in best-practice health and well-being programs?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-10(a & b), GRI 403-2(a), Embankment Project. Participating employees / total employees x 100.

questions.text: What is the employee absentee rate?
questions.hint: Health and well-being · Source: GRI 403-10(a & b), GRI 403-2(a), Embankment Project. Absentee rate = days lost / total days scheduled to be worked x 100, all employees.

disclosures.title: Skills for the future: Number of unfilled 'skilled' positions (#, %)

questions.text: How many skilled positions were unfilled at the end of the reporting period?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: WBCSD Measuring Impact Framework Methodology Version 1.0 (2008). Positions open for which no suitable skilled candidate was found.

questions.text: What percentage of all skilled positions is unfilled?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: WBCSD Measuring Impact Framework Methodology Version 1.0 (2008). Unfilled skilled positions / total skilled positions x 100.

questions.text: For what percentage of unfilled skilled positions will your company hire unskilled candidates and train them?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: WBCSD Measuring Impact Framework Methodology Version 1.0 (2008). Unfilled skilled positions to be filled by hiring and training unskilled candidates / total unfilled skilled positions x 100.

questions.text: Which skilled roles are hardest to fill?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: WBCSD Measuring Impact Framework Methodology Version 1.0 (2008). Optional context: role types and reasons.

disclosures.title: Skills for the future: Monetized impacts of training - increased earning capacity as a result of training intervention (%, $)

questions.text: What was your company's total investment in training?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: OECD, United Nations, WDI 5.5. Total training spend; state currency.

questions.text: What was total payroll in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: OECD, United Nations, WDI 5.5. Same period and currency as the training spend.

questions.text: What is your training investment as a percentage of payroll?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: OECD, United Nations, WDI 5.5. Training investment / total payroll x 100.

questions.text: Has training led to increased revenue?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: OECD, United Nations, WDI 5.5. Answer yes if you measure it.

questions.text: Has training led to productivity gains?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: OECD, United Nations, WDI 5.5. Answer yes if you measure it.

questions.text: Has training led to higher employee engagement?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: OECD, United Nations, WDI 5.5. Answer yes if you measure it.

questions.text: Has training led to higher internal hire rates?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: OECD, United Nations, WDI 5.5. Answer yes if you measure it.

questions.text: How does your company measure the effectiveness of training?
questions.hint: Skills for the future · Source: OECD, United Nations, WDI 5.5. Describe the method and results, in % or monetary value.
